```{r}
#| label: config
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Primary occupancy model; to switch to another fit, change this path and rerun the marginal-effects, NMDS and post-hoc trait scripts on it so the figure and table paths below exist for it
model_path <- "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Occ_mod_98spp_prec_hinge_f2_inits_2026-11-08.rds"
# One habitat interaction per model: the primary model holds the precipitation interaction, the other two are fitted separately with the same structure; distance to the forest edge is hinge-coded (Dist_open outside forest, Dist_inside inside it)
interaction_paths <- c(
  Tot_prec = model_path,
  Dist_forest = "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Occ_mod_98spp_dist_hinge_f2_inits_2026-11-08.rds",
  Year1 = "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Occ_mod_98spp_year_hinge_f2_inits_2026-11-08.rds"
)
# Habitat-specific slope of silvopasture cover within 300 m (all 209 locations), with forest cover within 300 m held; read from the fit's saved summary (community draws) rather than the ~2 GB fit
hab_ssp_summary_path <- "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Occ_mod_98spp_hab_ssp_f2_inits_2026-11-09_summary.rds"
# Primary model with silvopasture split into live fence and dispersed trees (habitat occupancy and NMDS): the fit, its saved summary (for the among-species variances) and the per-species live fence vs dispersed trees table extracted from the fit
split_model_path <- "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Occ_mod_98spp_split_hinge_f2_inits_2026-11-15.rds"
split_summary_path <- "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Occ_mod_98spp_split_hinge_f2_inits_2026-11-15_summary.rds"
# Species with P(live fence > dispersed trees) at or above this value, or at or below one minus it, are named in the text
split_p_strong <- 0.9
# Stacked list the multi-season list was built from (one row per surveyed location x survey period), for the data summary
stacked_list_path <- "Derived/Rdata/Model_input/Stacked/msOcc_l_meta_98_hab_fix_jit1cm.rds"
traits_path <- "../Fd-pd/Derived/Functional_traits_ch1.csv"
# Habitats are compared at a distance to the forest edge each one's data support, as in the marginal-effects figures: pasture and silvopasture at this shared distance outside forest (m; inside both habitats' interquartile ranges, while no pasture point lies closer than ~33 m to forest), forest at its median depth inside forest (computed below)
ref_open_m <- 100
# Trait-model summaries for both contrasts (silvopasture vs pasture, silvopasture vs forest)
posthoc_path <- paste0("Derived/Excels/postHoc_traits_", sub("\\.rds$", "", basename(model_path)), ".csv")
nmds_cache_path <- "Derived/Rdata/nmds/nmds_habitat_temporal_split_hinge_f2_inits_98_posterior_K50_dim3_distavg.rds"
# Species counted inside each habitat ellipse of the NMDS figure, written by the NMDS script
nmds_counts_path <- "Derived/Excels/nmds_ellipse_counts_temporal_split_hinge_f2_inits_98.csv"
# Species outside all four ellipses re-counted against the ellipses enlarged nmds_wide_scale times (not plotted), also written by the NMDS script
nmds_wide_scale <- 2
nmds_outside_path <- paste0("Derived/Excels/nmds_ellipse_counts_outside_x", nmds_wide_scale, "_temporal_split_hinge_f2_inits_98.csv")
fig_paths <- c(
  # Sampling map exports from the map script: Colombia context map, Meta inset and their shared legend
  map_colombia = "Figures/Map_sampling/Map_sampling_meta_colombia.png",
  map_inset = "Figures/Map_sampling/Map_sampling_meta_inset.png",
  map_legend = "Figures/Map_sampling/Map_sampling_meta_legend.png",
  habitat = "Figures/Marginal_effects/Hinge_models/marginal_temporal_split_hinge_f2_habitat_split.png",
  # Interaction figures from the marginal-effects script, one per goal: context (precipitation, distance), time, silvopasture cover within 300 m
  context = "Figures/Marginal_effects/Hinge_models/marginal_context_panel.png",
  time = "Figures/Marginal_effects/Hinge_models/marginal_time_panel.png",
  ssp_cover = "Figures/Marginal_effects/Hinge_models/marginal_ssp_cover_panel.png",
  nmds = "Figures/NMDS_meta/nmds_habitat_temporal_split_hinge_f2_inits_98_posterior_no_text.png"
)
# include_graphics() below skips its own existence check (it resolves paths from the project root, pandoc from this file's folder), so check here
if (!all(file.exists(fig_paths))) stop("Missing figure(s): ", paste(fig_paths[!file.exists(fig_paths)], collapse = ", "))
# NMDS draws with stress at or below the first value (degenerate) or above the second (not interpretable) are dropped, as in the NMDS script
nmds_stress_limits <- c(0.01, 0.2)
# Trait coefficients with P(>0) at or above this value, or at or below one minus it, are highlighted in the trait figure
trait_p_strong <- 0.9

habitat_labels <- c(Pastizales = "Pasture", Ssp = "Silvopasture", Bosque = "Forest")
split_labels <- c(Pastizales = "Pasture", Live_fence = "Live fence", Dispersed_trees = "Dispersed trees", Bosque = "Forest")
covariate_labels <- c(Tot_prec = "annual precipitation", Dist_forest = "distance to the forest edge", Year1 = "survey year")
migration_labels <- c(Long_distance = "Long-distance migrant", Partial = "Partial migrant", Sedentary = "Resident")
```

```{r}
#| label: extract-fits
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr interaction_paths
# The cache key includes the fit paths, so switching models re-extracts rather than reusing the old fits
# Keep only the pieces of each fit the report needs, since each fit is ~2 GB
extract_fit <- function(path) {
  fit <- readRDS(path)
  out <- list(
    beta_comm = as.matrix(fit$beta.comm.samples), beta = as.matrix(fit$beta.samples), rhat_comm = fit$rhat$beta.comm,
    n_factors = ncol(as.matrix(fit$lambda.samples)) / length(fit$sp.names), n_post = fit$n.post, n_chains = fit$n.chains,
    y = fit$y, sp_names = fit$sp.names
  )
  rm(fit); gc()
  out
}
fits <- map(interaction_paths, extract_fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: extract-split-fit
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr split_model_path
split_fit <- extract_fit(split_model_path)
```

```{r}
#| label: summaries
fit <- fits$Tot_prec
stacked <- readRDS(stacked_list_path)
Ft <- read_csv(traits_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(Species = str_replace(Species_ayerbe, " ", "_"))

# Formatting helpers: posterior mean with 95% CrI, and the posterior probability that a quantity is positive
fmt_ci <- function(x, digits = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (95%% CrI %.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"), mean(x), quantile(x, 0.025), quantile(x, 0.975))
fmt_p <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", mean(x > 0))
# Year-group codes ("13-14", "19") to calendar years ("2013-14", "2019")
year_label <- function(code) str_replace_all(code, "(^|-)(\\d{2})", "\\120\\2") %>% str_replace("-20", "-")

## Data scope
covs <- as_tibble(stacked$occ.covs)
n_locations <- n_distinct(covs$Id_survey_no_dc)
locations_by_habitat <- covs %>% distinct(Id_survey_no_dc, Habitat) %>% count(Habitat)
n_loc_hab <- setNames(locations_by_habitat$n, locations_by_habitat$Habitat)
n_visits <- sum(!is.na(stacked$y[1, , ]))
n_periods <- n_distinct(paste(covs$Year_grp, covs$Season))
years <- range(as.numeric(paste0("20", str_extract(covs$Year_grp, "^\\d{2}"))), as.numeric(paste0("20", str_extract(covs$Year_grp, "\\d{2}$"))))
n_species <- length(fit$sp_names)
min_detections <- min(apply(fit$y, 1, sum, na.rm = TRUE))

## Reference distances on the hinge terms' scale (metres divided by the distance-to-forest SD): pasture and silvopasture at ref_open_m outside forest, forest at its median depth over the surveyed forest location-year-groups
dist_scaling <- read_csv(str_replace(stacked_list_path, "\\.rds$", "_scaling.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(Process == "occupancy", Covariate == "Dist_forest")
source("Scripts/spOcc_fns.R")
ref_depth_m <- forest_reference_depth(covs$Dist_forest * dist_scaling$SD + dist_scaling$Mean, covs$Habitat == "Bosque", covs$Id_survey, covs$Year_grp)
d_open <- ref_open_m / dist_scaling$SD
d_in <- ref_depth_m / dist_scaling$SD
# Caption wording for the distance reference
dist_ref_text <- paste0("pasture and silvopasture ", ref_open_m, " m from the forest edge and forest at its median depth inside forest (", round(ref_depth_m), " m)")

## Community-level habitat effects (logit scale; relative to pasture, other covariates at their means); forest contrasts compare forest at its reference depth with the open habitats at their reference distance
bc <- fit$beta_comm
ssp_vs_pasture <- bc[, "HabitatSsp"]
forest_vs_pasture <- bc[, "HabitatBosque"] + d_in * bc[, "Dist_inside"] - d_open * bc[, "Dist_open"]
ssp_vs_forest <- ssp_vs_pasture - forest_vs_pasture
max_rhat_comm <- max(map_dbl(fits, \(f) max(f$rhat_comm)))

## Community-average predicted occupancy in each habitat: per draw, the mean across species of each species' predicted probability (as in the marginal-effects figures)
coef_draws <- function(term) fit$beta[, paste0(term, "-", fit$sp_names)]
b0 <- coef_draws("(Intercept)")
occ_hab <- list(
  Pasture = rowMeans(plogis(b0 + d_open * coef_draws("Dist_open"))),
  Silvopasture = rowMeans(plogis(b0 + coef_draws("HabitatSsp") + d_open * coef_draws("Dist_open"))),
  Forest = rowMeans(plogis(b0 + coef_draws("HabitatBosque") + d_in * coef_draws("Dist_inside")))
)

## Species-level silvopasture effects with the number of visits with a detection
ssp_sp <- coef_draws("HabitatSsp")
species_tbl <- tibble(
  Species = fit$sp_names, Mean = colMeans(ssp_sp), Lower = apply(ssp_sp, 2, quantile, 0.025), Upper = apply(ssp_sp, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  P_positive = colMeans(ssp_sp > 0), N_det = apply(fit$y, 1, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
) %>%
  left_join(select(Ft, Species, Migration_avo, Iucn_red_list), by = "Species") %>%
  mutate(Width = Upper - Lower, Migration = migration_labels[Migration_avo], Species_label = str_replace(Species, "_", " "))
n_sp_pos <- sum(species_tbl$Lower > 0)
n_sp_neg <- sum(species_tbl$Upper < 0)
# Partial pooling: compare interval widths and distance from the community mean between the least- and most-detected species
det_split <- median(species_tbl$N_det)
width_low <- median(species_tbl$Width[species_tbl$N_det < det_split])
width_high <- median(species_tbl$Width[species_tbl$N_det >= det_split])
sp_line <- function(sp) with(filter(species_tbl, Species == sp), sprintf("%.2f (95%% CrI %.2f to %.2f; P(>0) = %.2f; %d visits with a detection)", Mean, Lower, Upper, P_positive, N_det))
migrants <- filter(species_tbl, Migration_avo == "Long_distance") %>% arrange(desc(Mean))
# Near Threatened or above, other than the Blackpoll Warbler, which has its own sentence
threatened <- filter(species_tbl, Iucn_red_list != "LC", Species != "Setophaga_striata")
striata_rank <- rank(-species_tbl$Mean)[species_tbl$Species == "Setophaga_striata"]
# First survey year of pasture, and the silvopasture location-periods surveyed before it, for the data-scope sentence
start_year <- as.numeric(paste0("20", str_extract(covs$Year_grp, "^\\d{2}")))
first_pasture_year <- min(start_year[covs$Habitat == "Pastizales"])
ssp_early <- covs$Habitat == "Ssp" & start_year < first_pasture_year
n_ssp_early <- sum(ssp_early)
ssp_early_years <- knitr::combine_words(year_label(sort(unique(covs$Year_grp[ssp_early]))))

## Habitat interactions, each from its own model
interaction_draws <- imap(fits, \(f, cov) if (cov == "Dist_forest") {
  # Hinge coding: pasture's slope with distance outside forest, silvopasture's difference from it, and forest's slope with depth inside forest
  list(pasture = f$beta_comm[, "Dist_open"], ssp = f$beta_comm[, "Ssp_Dist_open"], inside = f$beta_comm[, "Dist_inside"])
} else {
  list(pasture = f$beta_comm[, cov], ssp = f$beta_comm[, paste0("HabitatSsp:", cov)], forest = f$beta_comm[, paste0("HabitatBosque:", cov)])
})
# SD of each occupancy covariate in its original units, so slopes can be stated per SD (precipitation in mm, distance in m, year in years, silvopasture cover in percentage points); the hinge distance terms are in units of the distance-to-forest SD, without centring
occ_sd <- read_csv(str_replace(stacked_list_path, "\\.rds$", "_scaling.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(Process == "occupancy") %>%
  pull(SD, name = Covariate)

## Silvopasture cover within 300 m, by habitat (the pasture slope plus each habitat's difference from it), per SD of silvopasture cover (percentage points)
hab_ssp <- readRDS(hab_ssp_summary_path)

## Silvopasture split into live fence and dispersed trees (logit scale, relative to pasture), and the among-species variance of each effect
split <- readRDS(split_summary_path)
split_bc <- split_fit$beta_comm
lf_vs_pasture <- split_bc[, "Habitat_splitLive_fence"]
dt_vs_pasture <- split_bc[, "Habitat_splitDispersed_trees"]
split_forest_vs_pasture <- split_bc[, "Habitat_splitBosque"] + d_in * split_bc[, "Dist_inside"] - d_open * split_bc[, "Dist_open"]
lf_vs_dt <- lf_vs_pasture - dt_vs_pasture
lf_vs_forest <- lf_vs_pasture - split_forest_vs_pasture
dt_vs_forest <- dt_vs_pasture - split_forest_vs_pasture
# Community-average predicted occupancy in each habitat, as for the primary model above
split_coef <- function(term) split_fit$beta[, paste0(term, "-", split_fit$sp_names)]
split_b0 <- split_coef("(Intercept)")
split_open <- d_open * split_coef("Dist_open")
occ_split <- list(
  Pasture = rowMeans(plogis(split_b0 + split_open)),
  Live_fence = rowMeans(plogis(split_b0 + split_coef("Habitat_splitLive_fence") + split_open)),
  Dispersed_trees = rowMeans(plogis(split_b0 + split_coef("Habitat_splitDispersed_trees") + split_open)),
  Forest = rowMeans(plogis(split_b0 + split_coef("Habitat_splitBosque") + d_in * split_coef("Dist_inside")))
)
split_tau_median <- apply(split$draws$tau.sq.beta[, c("Habitat_splitLive_fence", "Habitat_splitDispersed_trees")], 2, median)
# Per-species difference between live fence and dispersed trees (logit), from each species' two coefficients
lf_dt_sp <- split_coef("Habitat_splitLive_fence") - split_coef("Habitat_splitDispersed_trees")
split_species <- tibble(Species = split_fit$sp_names, LFminusDT_lo = apply(lf_dt_sp, 2, quantile, 0.025), LFminusDT_hi = apply(lf_dt_sp, 2, quantile, 0.975), P_LF_gt_DT = colMeans(lf_dt_sp > 0))
n_sp_lf_gt_dt <- sum(split_species$LFminusDT_lo > 0)
n_sp_dt_gt_lf <- sum(split_species$LFminusDT_hi < 0)
sp_italic <- function(sp) as.character(knitr::combine_words(paste0("*", str_replace(sp, "_", " "), "*")))
# Species leaning clearly towards one type, strongest first; those whose 95% CrI of the difference excludes zero are marked with an asterisk
split_lean <- function(favours_lf) {
  x <- if (favours_lf) filter(split_species, P_LF_gt_DT >= split_p_strong) %>% arrange(desc(P_LF_gt_DT)) else filter(split_species, P_LF_gt_DT <= 1 - split_p_strong) %>% arrange(P_LF_gt_DT)
  x <- mutate(x, Clear = LFminusDT_lo > 0 | LFminusDT_hi < 0, Text = paste0("*", str_replace(Species, "_", " "), "*", if_else(Clear, "\\*", ""), " (P = ", sprintf("%.2f", if (favours_lf) P_LF_gt_DT else 1 - P_LF_gt_DT), ")"))
  list(n = nrow(x), text = as.character(knitr::combine_words(x$Text)))
}
lean_lf <- split_lean(TRUE)
lean_dt <- split_lean(FALSE)
hab_ssp_bc <- hab_ssp$draws$beta.comm
max_rhat_comm <- max(max_rhat_comm, hab_ssp$max_comm_rhat)
ssp_cover_slopes <- list(
  pasture = hab_ssp_bc[, "ssp"],
  ssp = hab_ssp_bc[, "ssp"] + hab_ssp_bc[, "HabitatSsp:ssp"],
  forest = hab_ssp_bc[, "ssp"] + hab_ssp_bc[, "HabitatBosque:ssp"]
)

## Post-hoc trait models
posthoc_all <- read_csv(posthoc_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
# The text's main numbers are for silvopasture vs pasture; silvopasture vs forest gets its own summary below
posthoc <- filter(posthoc_all, Contrast == "Ssp_vs_pasture")
posthoc_terms <- filter(posthoc, Term != "(Intercept)")
n_traits <- n_distinct(posthoc_terms$Trait)
n_trait_models <- n_distinct(posthoc_terms$Model)
n_trait_excl0 <- sum(posthoc_terms$Lower > 0 | posthoc_terms$Upper < 0)
# Display labels for the trait terms, used in the text and the trait figure
term_labels <- c(
  Body_size = "Body size (PC1 of mass, tail, tarsus)", HWI = "Hand-wing index", Beak_size = "Beak size (PC1)", Beak_shape = "Beak shape (PC2)",
  Eye_resid = "Eye size relative to body size",
  Habitat.DensityOpen = "Open habitat (vs. dense)", Habitat.DensitySemi_open = "Semi-open habitat (vs. dense)", Migration_avoLong_distance = "Long-distance migrant (vs. resident)", Migration_avoPartial = "Partial migrant (vs. resident)",
  Trophic.LevelHerbivore = "Herbivore (vs. carnivore)", Trophic.LevelOmnivore = "Omnivore (vs. carnivore)", Gen_length = "Generation length",
  Elev_range = "Elevational range", Range.Size = "Geographic range size", Forest_specialization = "Forest specialization", Habitat_breadth = "Habitat breadth", Diet_breadth = "Diet breadth",
  Clutch_mean = "Clutch size", Nest_ground_bushTRUE = "Nests on the ground or in bushes", N_nest_locs_sheard = "Number of nest sites used", Nest_exposure = "Nest enclosure (open to enclosed)"
)
# Coefficients with a clear tendency (coloured in the trait figure), strongest first, as "label (mean, CrI; P(>0))" phrases for the text
strong_traits <- posthoc_terms %>%
  filter(P_positive >= trait_p_strong | P_positive <= 1 - trait_p_strong) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(P_positive - 0.5))) %>%
  mutate(Label = str_replace(term_labels[Term], "^(\\w)", tolower), Text = sprintf("%s (%.2f, 95%% CrI %.2f to %.2f; P(>0) = %.2f)", Label, Mean, Lower, Upper, P_positive))
# The Takeaways sentence on traits names these two positive tendencies in words, so stop if the trait results change
stopifnot(setequal(strong_traits$Term, c("Habitat.DensitySemi_open", "Diet_breadth")), all(strong_traits$P_positive >= trait_p_strong))
# Model names with their species counts, for the trait figure caption
model_labels <- c(Morphology = "morphology", Eye_size = "eye size", Life_history = "life history", Specialization = "specialization", Clutch_size = "clutch size", Nest_location = "nest location", Nest_exposure = "nest enclosure")
model_n_text <- distinct(posthoc, Model, N_species) %>% with(paste0(model_labels[Model], " ", N_species))
# Silvopasture vs forest: the same models, strong tendencies as phrases for the text
posthoc_forest <- filter(posthoc_all, Contrast == "Ssp_vs_forest")
posthoc_forest_terms <- filter(posthoc_forest, Term != "(Intercept)")
n_trait_excl0_forest <- sum(posthoc_forest_terms$Lower > 0 | posthoc_forest_terms$Upper < 0)
strong_traits_forest <- posthoc_forest_terms %>%
  filter(P_positive >= trait_p_strong | P_positive <= 1 - trait_p_strong) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(P_positive - 0.5))) %>%
  mutate(Label = str_replace(term_labels[Term], "^(\\w)", tolower), Text = sprintf("%s (%.2f, 95%% CrI %.2f to %.2f; P(>0) = %.2f)", Label, Mean, Lower, Upper, P_positive))

## NMDS
nmds <- readRDS(nmds_cache_path)
draw_stress <- map_dbl(nmds$nmds_draws, "stress")
n_nmds_kept <- sum(draw_stress > nmds_stress_limits[1] & draw_stress <= nmds_stress_limits[2])
# Species whose (posterior-mean) NMDS score lies inside each habitat's bold ellipse, species inside two or more ellipses counted in each overlap, and outside all four
nmds_counts <- read_csv(nmds_counts_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
n_sp_only <- map_int(set_names(unname(split_labels)), \(h) sum(nmds_counts$As_plotted[nmds_counts$Class == h]))
# One phrase per overlap that holds any species, e.g. '2 inside both the pasture and silvopasture ellipses'
nmds_shared_text <- nmds_counts %>%
  filter(str_detect(Class, fixed("+")), As_plotted > 0) %>%
  mutate(Habitats = map_chr(str_split(tolower(Class), fixed(" + ")), \(x) as.character(knitr::combine_words(x))), Text = paste0(As_plotted, " inside ", if_else(str_count(Class, fixed("+")) == 1, "both ", "all of "), "the ", Habitats, " ellipses")) %>%
  pull(Text)
n_sp_none <- sum(nmds_counts$As_plotted[nmds_counts$Class == "None"])
nmds_outside <- read_csv(nmds_outside_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(sum(nmds_outside$As_plotted) == n_sp_none)
# Count, and percentage of those now inside any enlarged ellipse, for one ellipse class (0 when absent)
n_outside_in <- sum(nmds_outside$As_plotted[nmds_outside$Class != "None"])
n_wide <- \(class) sum(nmds_outside$As_plotted[nmds_outside$Class == class])
pct_wide <- \(class) round(100 * n_wide(class) / n_outside_in)
# One phrase per enlarged-ellipse class holding any species, largest first, e.g. '45% within the forest ellipse only'
nmds_wide_text <- nmds_outside %>%
  filter(Class != "None", As_plotted > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(As_plotted)) %>%
  mutate(Habitats = map_chr(str_split(tolower(Class), fixed(" + ")), \(x) as.character(knitr::combine_words(x))), Text = paste0(round(100 * As_plotted / n_outside_in), "% within ", if_else(str_detect(Class, fixed("+")), paste0("the ", Habitats, " ellipses"), paste0("the ", Habitats, " ellipse only")))) %>%
  pull(Text)
```

## Background and goals

Silvopastoral systems, which combine trees and shrubs with pasture, are promoted in Colombia as a way to make cattle ranching more productive while retaining biodiversity. This report summarizes recent results on how bird occupancy and community composition in silvopasture compare with those in conventional monoculture pasture and in forest. It has five goals: (1) to estimate how occupancy differs among monoculture pasture, silvopasture and forest; (2) to ask whether the advantage of silvopasture depends on its climatic and landscape context (annual precipitation and distance to the forest edge); (3) to ask whether silvopasture has maintained bird occupancy over the survey period, relative to pasture and forest; (4) to ask whether silvopasture in the surrounding landscape (within 300 m) raises occupancy in nearby monoculture pasture and forest; and (5) to describe how community composition differs among the three habitats.

The data come from the Sustainable Cattle Ranching project and partner monitoring in the department of Meta only (@fig-map): `r n_locations` unique point-count locations (`r n_loc_hab["Pastizales"]` in pasture, `r n_loc_hab["Ssp"]` in silvopasture and `r n_loc_hab["Bosque"]` in forest) surveyed across `r n_periods` survey periods between `r years[1]` and `r years[2]`, for `r format(n_visits, big.mark = ",")` point-count visits in total. Each period is one year group, split into an early and a late round where a location was revisited more than 80 days after its first visit; the habitats surveyed changed over time (@tbl-scope), and pasture and silvopasture were surveyed almost only from `r first_pasture_year` onwards (silvopasture also at `r n_ssp_early` location-periods in `r ssp_early_years`), whereas forest spans the whole period.

I fit a hierarchical multi-species occupancy model to the `r n_species` species detected on at least `r min_detections` visits (done to keep models manageable for runs on my laptop). Each species has its own coefficients, drawn from a community-level distribution, so species with few detections borrow strength from the community (partial pooling). Occupancy was modeled as a function of habitat, annual precipitation, distance to the forest edge, the proportion of silvopasture within 300 m and survey year, with a spatial random effect built from `r fit$n_factors` latent spatial factors linking nearby locations. Interactions were included in separate models to address goals 2-4. Detection depends on whether the point is in forest, start time of the point count, the probability of breeding activity on the survey date, the day of the survey and the observer team as a random effect. Each habitat interaction was fitted in its own model. All models were fitted in a Bayesian framework (`r fit$n_chains` chains, `r format(fit$n_chains * fit$n_post, big.mark = ",")` posterior draws kept per model); all community-level parameters had Rhat ≤ `r sprintf("%.2f", max_rhat_comm)`. Effects are given as posterior means with 95% credible intervals (CrI) on the logit (log-odds) scale, with the posterior probability that the effect is positive, i.e. P(\>0).

```{r}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-cap: "Point-count locations in Meta, Colombia. Left: Colombia's departments, with Meta outlined in red, the main rivers in blue and an inset map of sampling locations (black box). Elevation is on a log scale. Right: point-count locations, by data collector (symbol) and number of locations in each 0.015° cell (symbol size), jittered so that neighbouring cells do not overlap; elevation on a linear scale."

# Join the three map exports side by side at a common height; the legend is padded rather than enlarged
map_imgs <- map(fig_paths[c("map_colombia", "map_inset", "map_legend")], magick::image_read)
map_height <- max(map_dbl(map_imgs, \(img) magick::image_info(img)$height))
map_panels <- c(magick::image_scale(map_imgs$map_colombia, paste0("x", map_height)), magick::image_scale(map_imgs$map_inset, paste0("x", map_height)), magick::image_extent(map_imgs$map_legend, paste0(magick::image_info(map_imgs$map_legend)$width + 60, "x", map_height), gravity = "center", color = "white"))

map_px <- as.integer(magick::image_data(map_panels[1], "rgb"))
is_black <- map_px[, , 1] < 40 & map_px[, , 2] < 40 & map_px[, , 3] < 40
longest_run <- \(v) { r <- rle(v); max(c(0, r$lengths[r$values])) }
box_rows <- range(which(apply(is_black, 1, longest_run) >= 0.9 * max(apply(is_black, 1, longest_run))))
box_right <- max(which(apply(is_black, 2, longest_run) >= 0.9 * max(apply(is_black, 2, longest_run))))
panel_left <- magick::image_info(map_panels[1])$width
map_fig <- magick::image_draw(magick::image_append(map_panels))
segments(box_right, box_rows, panel_left, c(0, map_height - 1), col = "black", lwd = 4)
invisible(dev.off())
magick::image_write(map_fig, map_file)
include_graphics(file.path("../..", map_file), error = FALSE)
```

## Occupancy in pasture, silvopasture and forest

Occupancy was higher in both silvopasture types than in monoculture pasture for the community as a whole. In the model with silvopasture split into live fences and dispersed trees, the community-mean effect relative to pasture was `r fmt_ci(lf_vs_pasture)` for live fences (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(lf_vs_pasture)`), `r fmt_ci(dt_vs_pasture)` for dispersed trees (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(dt_vs_pasture)`) and `r fmt_ci(split_forest_vs_pasture)` for forest (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(split_forest_vs_pasture)`). Both silvopasture types remained below forest (live fences minus forest `r fmt_ci(lf_vs_forest)`; dispersed trees minus forest `r fmt_ci(dt_vs_forest)`), and the two types did not clearly differ from each other (live fences minus dispersed trees `r fmt_ci(lf_vs_dt)`; P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(lf_vs_dt)`). On the probability scale, the mean predicted occupancy across species was `r fmt_ci(occ_split$Pasture)` in pasture, `r fmt_ci(occ_split$Live_fence)` in live fences, `r fmt_ci(occ_split$Dispersed_trees)` in dispersed trees and `r fmt_ci(occ_split$Forest)` in forest (@fig-habitat).

Species differed far more in their response to dispersed trees than to live fences: the among-species variance of the habitat effect was `r sprintf('%.2f', split_tau_median[2])` for dispersed trees but `r sprintf('%.2f', split_tau_median[1])` for live fences. Live fences thus raised occupancy relative to pasture by a similar amount for most species, so each species' live-fence effect is estimated close to the community mean, whereas dispersed trees favoured some species and not others. Comparing the two types species by species, `r lean_dt$n` species were more likely to occupy dispersed trees than live fences (posterior probability of higher occupancy in dispersed trees of at least `r split_p_strong`): `r lean_dt$text`. Another `r lean_lf$n` were more likely to occupy live fences: `r lean_lf$text`. An asterisk marks the species whose 95% CrI of the difference excluded zero.

```{r}
#| label: fig-habitat
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Mean predicted occupancy probability across bird species in monoculture pasture, the two silvopasture types (live fences and dispersed trees) and forest, from the primary model with silvopasture split by type. Coloured points are posterior means and bars are 95% credible intervals of the mean across species of each species' predicted occupancy, with ", dist_ref_text, ", other covariates held at their means and the spatial effect at zero. Grey points are the posterior means of individual species.")
#| out-width: "85%"
include_graphics(file.path("../..", fig_paths["habitat"]), error = FALSE)
```

Species-level effects varied around this community mean. For `r n_sp_pos` of `r n_species` species the 95% CrI of the silvopasture effect lay entirely above zero, and for `r n_sp_neg` entirely below. The Blackpoll Warbler (*Setophaga striata*), a Nearctic-Neotropical migrant listed as Near Threatened, had `r if (striata_rank == 1) "the largest" else paste("the", scales::ordinal(striata_rank), "largest")` silvopasture effect of the `r n_species` species: `r sp_line("Setophaga_striata")`. The other species listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN: `r paste0("*", threatened$Species_label, "* (", threatened$Iucn_red_list, "): ", map_chr(threatened$Species, sp_line), collapse = "; ")`. Posterior means of the `r nrow(migrants)` long-distance migrants in the model were `r paste0("*", migrants$Species_label, "* (", sprintf("%.2f", migrants$Mean), ")", collapse = ", ")`. It is important to note that the model pools information across species, thus each species' estimate is pulled towards the community mean, with stronger partial pooling in data-sparse species.

Species are ranked by effect, continuing from the left panel to the right. The solid vertical line is the community mean and the dashed line zero effect. Species detected on few visits are pulled towards the community mean by partial pooling, so their intervals are wide."

## Does the effect of silvopasture depend on context?

Each habitat interaction was fit in a separate model.`r if (fits$Year1$n_factors != fit$n_factors) paste0(" The habitat-by-year model is an earlier fit with ", fits$Year1$n_factors, " spatial factors rather than ", fit$n_factors, " and distance to the forest edge as a single linear term; a refit matching the other models is running.") else ""` Per 1 SD of annual precipitation (`r round(occ_sd["Tot_prec"])` mm), the slope of occupancy was `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Tot_prec$ssp)` steeper in silvopasture than in pasture (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(interaction_draws$Tot_prec$ssp)`), whereas in forest the slope did not show strong directionality (`r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Tot_prec$forest)`; @fig-context a). Per 1 SD of distance from the forest edge (`r round(occ_sd["Dist_forest"])` m), occupancy declined in pasture (slope `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Dist_forest$pasture)`), and the decline in silvopasture was similar (difference from pasture `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Dist_forest$ssp)`; P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(interaction_draws$Dist_forest$ssp)`); inside forest, occupancy `r if (mean(interaction_draws$Dist_forest$inside) < 0) "declined" else "rose"` with depth from the forest edge (slope `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Dist_forest$inside)`; @fig-context b).

Distance to the forest edge entered as a piecewise linear effect with a fixed breakpoint at the forest edge, allowing separate slopes outside and inside forest and a habitat-specific step at the edge. Each curve spans the values observed in that habitat; other covariates are held at their means, with ", dist_ref_text, " in (a). Interactions were fit in separate models to improve sampling and convergence.")

## Has silvopasture maintained occupancy over time?

Communities are expected to pay an extinction debt in fragmented landscapes. Per 1 SD of survey year (`r round(occ_sd["Year1"], 1)` years), occupancy in pasture declined (slope `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Year1$pasture)`), while occupancy in silvopasture and forest was relatively stable over the study period (difference from the pasture slope: silvopasture `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Year1$ssp)`, P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(interaction_draws$Year1$ssp)`; forest `r fmt_ci(interaction_draws$Year1$forest)`, P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(interaction_draws$Year1$forest)`; @fig-time).

Each curve spans the values observed in that habitat; other covariates are held at their means, with ", dist_ref_text, ".")
```{r}
#| out-width: "70%"
include_graphics(file.path("../..", fig_paths["time"]), error = FALSE)
```

## Does silvopasture benefit pasture and forest?

Does silvopasture in the surrounding landscape benefit birds in nearby pasture and forest? A separate model let the effect of silvopasture cover within 300 m differ by habitat, holding forest cover within 300 m constant, so that more silvopasture nearby means less pasture rather than less forest (all `r hab_ssp$n_sites` locations). Per 1 SD of silvopasture cover (`r round(occ_sd["ssp"])`%), occupancy rose in pasture (`r fmt_ci(ssp_cover_slopes$pasture)`; P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(ssp_cover_slopes$pasture)`), but hardly changed in silvopasture (`r fmt_ci(ssp_cover_slopes$ssp)`; P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(ssp_cover_slopes$ssp)`) and tended to decline in forest (`r fmt_ci(ssp_cover_slopes$forest)`; P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(ssp_cover_slopes$forest)`; @fig-ssp-cover). So silvopasture nearby appears to spill over into monoculture pasture, but there is no evidence that it buffers forest. Pasture points with silvopasture nearby are on farms that adopted silvopasture, so this may partly reflect other differences between adopting and non-adopting farms.

Each curve spans the values observed in that habitat; other covariates are held at their means, with ", dist_ref_text, ", and forest cover within 300 m at its mean.")
```{r}
#| out-width: "70%"
include_graphics(file.path("../..", fig_paths["ssp_cover"]), error = FALSE)
```

## Community composition

Communities differed in composition among the four habitats, which were ordered along the first axis from pasture through live fences and dispersed trees to forest; live-fence communities overlapped pasture more than dispersed-tree communities did (@fig-nmds). The ordination is built from the model's estimated presence or absence of every species at each surveyed location and period, therefore accounting for heterogeneity in detection probability. It is repeated on `r length(draw_stress)` posterior draws to carry their uncertainty; `r n_nmds_kept` draws had interpretable solutions (stress between `r nmds_stress_limits[1]` and `r nmds_stress_limits[2]`), and the reference solution had a stress of `r sprintf("%.2f", nmds$nmds_ref$stress)`. When the ellipses in @fig-nmds are enlarged to `r nmds_wide_scale` SD (not shown), `r n_outside_in` of the `r n_sp_none` species that are currently outside all four ellipses fall within at least one: `r knitr::combine_words(nmds_wide_text)`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-nmds
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS; Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, three dimensions, first two shown) of bird communities at each surveyed location and period, coloured by habitat, from the primary model with silvopasture split into live fences and dispersed trees. Ellipses show one standard deviation of location scores for each habitat, drawn for each of the ", n_nmds_kept, " retained posterior draws after aligning each draw's ordination to a reference solution by Procrustes rotation. Crosses represent the expanded weighted averages of the scores of the locations where each species is estimated to be present; larger crosses mark the pictured species. Of the ", sum(nmds_counts$As_plotted), " species, ", n_sp_only["Pasture"], " lie only inside the pasture ellipse, ", n_sp_only["Live fence"], " only inside the live-fence ellipse, ", n_sp_only["Dispersed trees"], " only inside the dispersed-tree ellipse and ", n_sp_only["Forest"], " only inside the forest ellipse; ", if (length(nmds_shared_text) > 0) paste0(knitr::combine_words(nmds_shared_text), ", and ") else "", n_sp_none, " outside all four.")
#| out-width: "100%"
include_graphics(file.path("../..", fig_paths["nmds"]), error = FALSE)
```

## Which species respond most to silvopasture? Trait models

To ask whether species' traits explain their response to silvopasture, I regressed each species' silvopasture effect (relative to pasture) on its traits, carrying the full posterior of the occupancy model into each regression. I tested `r n_traits` traits in `r n_trait_models` models covering morphology, eye size, life history, ecological specialization, clutch size, nest location and nest enclosure (@fig-traits). `r if (n_trait_excl0 == 0) "No trait clearly explained species' responses: every coefficient's 95% CrI overlapped zero" else paste(n_trait_excl0, "of the", nrow(posthoc_terms), "coefficients had a 95% CrI excluding zero")`, and the models explained little variation (median Bayesian R² from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(posthoc$Bayes_R2))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(posthoc$Bayes_R2))`). The clearest tendencies, with P(\>0) ≥ `r trait_p_strong` or ≤ `r 1 - trait_p_strong` (coloured in @fig-traits), were `r knitr::combine_words(strong_traits$Text)`.

Because silvopasture is intermediate in structure between pasture and forest, I also regressed each species' silvopasture effect relative to forest (its predicted logit-scale occupancy in silvopasture minus that in forest within each posterior draw, with `r dist_ref_text`) on the same traits (@fig-traits b). `r if (n_trait_excl0_forest == 0) "No coefficient's 95% CrI excluded zero" else paste(n_trait_excl0_forest, "of the", nrow(posthoc_forest_terms), "coefficients had a 95% CrI excluding zero")` (median Bayesian R² from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(posthoc_forest$Bayes_R2))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(posthoc_forest$Bayes_R2))`); the clearest tendencies were `r knitr::combine_words(strong_traits_forest$Text)`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-traits
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Trait models of species' silvopasture effects relative to (a) pasture and (b) forest. Points and bars are the posterior mean and 95% credible interval of each coefficient, the change in a species' silvopasture effect (logit scale) per standard deviation of a continuous trait, or relative to the reference level of a categorical trait; positive values mean species with more of the trait fare better in silvopasture. Traits are grouped by model (", knitr::combine_words(model_n_text), " species, those with data for every trait in the model). Coefficients with P(>0) ≥ ", trait_p_strong, " or ≤ ", 1 - trait_p_strong, " are coloured.")
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-width: 7.5
contrast_labels <- c(Ssp_vs_pasture = "(a) Silvopasture vs. pasture", Ssp_vs_forest = "(b) Silvopasture vs. forest")
posthoc_all %>%
  filter(Term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(Contrast = factor(contrast_labels[Contrast], levels = contrast_labels),
         Model = fct_inorder(Model),
         Trait = fct_rev(fct_inorder(term_labels[Term])),
         Direction = case_when(P_positive >= trait_p_strong ~ "Positive", P_positive <= 1 - trait_p_strong ~ "Negative", .default = "Weak")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Mean, y = Trait, colour = Direction)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper), height = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  # One row block per trait model, separated by space instead of labelled strips; the caption names the models
  facet_grid(Model ~ Contrast, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Positive = "#2a78d6", Negative = "#c2410c", Weak = "grey55"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Change in silvopasture effect (log-odds)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_blank(), strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 9), panel.spacing.y = unit(6, "pt"), panel.spacing.x = unit(10, "pt"), panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey85"))
```

## Takeaways

- **Silvopasture supports more birds than monoculture pasture, but fewer than forest.** With pasture and silvopasture `r ref_open_m` m from the forest edge and forest at its median depth (`r round(ref_depth_m)` m), mean predicted occupancy across species was `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(occ_hab$Pasture))` in pasture, `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(occ_hab$Silvopasture))` in silvopasture and `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(occ_hab$Forest))` in forest (silvopasture vs. pasture P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(ssp_vs_pasture)`).
- **The benefit is broad but uneven across species.** `r n_sp_pos` of `r n_species` species had a clearly positive silvopasture effect and `r n_sp_neg` had a clearly negative one; the Near Threatened Blackpoll Warbler had `r if (striata_rank == 1) "the largest" else paste("the", scales::ordinal(striata_rank), "largest")` effect.
- **Context matters.** The benefit of silvopasture over pasture increased with annual precipitation (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(interaction_draws$Tot_prec$ssp)`), suggesting silvopasture may benefit biodiversity more in wetter climates than in more xeric ones. Occupancy fell with distance from the forest edge in both pasture and silvopasture at a similar rate, so proximity to forest raised occupancy in both habitats rather than the benefit of silvopasture specifically.
  - Mean occupancy across species is highest at the edge of forest fragments (@fig-context b).
  - More silvopasture within 300 m raised occupancy in nearby monoculture pasture (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(ssp_cover_slopes$pasture)`) but not in forest (P(\>0) = `r fmt_p(ssp_cover_slopes$forest)`).
- **Silvopasture communities are intermediate in composition between pasture and forest.** Silvopasture communities, particularly live fences, overlap pasture more than forest (@fig-nmds).
- **A species' preferred vegetation density, more than any other trait, shaped their response to silvopasture.** The strongest effects show that species affiliated with semi-open and open (just relative to forest) habitats benefited most from silvopasture. Species with flexible diets were also found more in silvopasture (compared to pasture).
  - Species with broader diets tended to benefit more from silvopasture than from pasture, suggesting that dietary generalists can exploit the mix of resources silvopasture offers. The trends regarding habitat density suggests that structural complexity is important in determining community composition.
  - Silvopasture is intermediate in habitat structure (and resources) relative to pasture and forest; thus, the contrast between traits would likely be largest if comparing pasture and forest (but that is beyond the scope of this paper). Another important possibility is that much of the bird community that was historically present in this system may have already been lost, and thus the traits observed in our study are from a non-random subset of the historical species pool.
